title: Prompt lifecycle iteration log
content:
Purpose:
A scratchpad to iterate on a small prompt library workflow: how prompts age, how few-shot exemplars are chosen and rotated, quick failure case cataloging, and lightweight evaluation rubrics. Goal is to end up with a repeatable pipeline for weekly prompt refreshes and a short checklist for moving a template to "stable".

Top-level hypothesis:
- Rotating exemplars across 3 cohorts reduces brittle overfitting to a small set of inputs and exposes regressions earlier.
- Explicit instruction scaffolding (short system + structured response schema) reduces format-related failures by ~30%.

Quick definitions (working):
- Template: canonical system+instruction+format spec.
- Few-shot set: up to 5 exemplars used inline.
- Cohort: a bucket of exemplars swapped on a cadence.
- Stable: template that has <5% format regressions across last 4 weeks.

Version notes / changelog:
- 2024-09-18: created; initial ideas for cohort rotation.
- 2024-10-02: tried rotating 2 exemplars per week — saw spike in hallucinations for extraction task.
- 2024-10-25: added structured output schema to reduce format drift.
- 2024-11-22: added short manual evaluation rubric and failure case catalog seed.

Rotation strategy (sketch):
- Maintain 3 cohorts A/B/C of exemplars per template. Each week swap which cohort is active inline; keep 1 exemplar fixed for stability.
- When a cohort consistently triggers an error pattern, move those exemplars to the pool for reannotation.
- Rationale: diversity + controlled stability.

Template draft: generic Q&A summarizer (for app internal use)
- System: "You are a concise summarizer that always returns JSON with fields: {summary, highlights, follow_ups}. summary is 2-3 sentences. highlights is a short bullet list. follow_ups is 0-3 suggested clarifying questions."
- Instruction (user): "Given the conversation below, produce the JSON. Keep language plain. Avoid adding new facts."
- Format schema (explicit):
  "summary": "string",
  "highlights": ["string"],
  "follow_ups": ["string"]

Few-shot exemplar set (Cohort A) — short examples: 
1) EX1_INPUT: "User: I can't login after the update. Support: Did you try resetting? User: it didn't work."
   EX1_OUTPUT: {summary: "User cannot login after update despite reset attempt.", highlights: ["failed reset","login broken post-update"], follow_ups: ["What device/OS?","Exact error message?"]}
2) EX2_INPUT: "User: app crashes when opening profile. Crash log shows NPE"
   EX2_OUTPUT: {...}

(These are intentionally terse in the scratchpad — full exemplars live in bench/bench-exemplars folder)

Failure case catalog (seed entries):
- Format drift: model returns text instead of JSON when conversation includes a multi-turn code block. Example input & bad output attached to ticket #47.
- Hallucinated follow-up: model fabricates a question referencing an entity not in the conversation.
- Over-truncation: summary leaves out the user’s main complaint when convo > 800 tokens.

Manual eval rubric (quick):
- Format correctness (0/1): returns valid JSON matching schema.
- Faithfulness (0-2): 0=contradiction, 1=partial, 2=faithful/no new facts.
- Usefulness (0-2): 0=useless, 1=some signal, 2=good actionable summary.
Scoring: pass if format==1 and faithfulness+usefulness >=3.

Automated checks to implement (shortlist):
- JSON schema validation on outputs.
- Token-length heuristic: if input > X, fall back to "short_summary" mode.
- Quick NER check: ensure follow_ups don't contain named entities not present in input.

Experiment ideas (next sprints):
1) Soft prompt vs explicit schema: ablate system message that enumerates fields vs removing it.
2) Few-shot diversity: compare fixed exemplar set vs rotating cohorts A/B/C over 4 weeks.
3) Exemplar augmentation: paraphrase exemplars with LM to increase variety then test drift.

Quick test cases to add to bench:
- Long conversation with repeated clarifications (should keep summary short).
- Conversation with code/config snippet (ensure JSON still returned).
- Conversation referencing dates/times (verify no temporal hallucination).

Open questions / TODOs:
- How often should "fixed" exemplar be updated? Hypothesis: monthly unless error rate increases.
- Thresholds for moving template to stable need to be defined in product terms (SLA?).
- Add a synthetic adversarial set that intentionally tries to break the JSON parser.

Integration notes (engineering):
- When moving a template to "stable", tag in prompt-store (prompt-store#release) and create a quick rollback spec.
- Add a small token accounting check to ensure few-shot additions won't blow costs.

Notes to self: keep iterations short (1-2 prompts changed per week). Prefer hand-annotating 10 failure examples before running larger auto-analysis.

Next actions (this week):
- [ ] Formalize JSON schema and add to bench tests (assigned: me).
- [ ] Spin up 3 cohort exemplar pools from existing bench (Samir will help).
- [ ] Run a quick A/B of explicit schema vs no-schema on 200 samples (Maya to run).

End of scratchpad.

Attachments / pointers (local):
- bench/exemplars/summarizer/cohort-a.csv (WIP)
- tickets: #47, #102 (format cases)
